MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, NOVEMBER 1, 2021

  A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
  order by CHAIR EDLER at 7:00 p.m. Pursuant to Assembly Bill 361, this meeting was held via
  teleconference.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR EDLER led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Edler, Carman, Medawar, Schachter, Scott, Yoo

  Commissioners Absent:  Zigrang

  City Staff Present:  David Wahba, Director of Community Development and Public Works
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  Also Present:  Kane Thuyen, Assistant City Attorney
  Joanne Itagaki, Traffic Engineering Deputy

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, OCTOBER 4, 2021

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT noted a change needed in the roll call.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER CARMAN to,

  APPROVE THE CORRECTED PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF
  OCTOBER 4, 2021.

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  NONE

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  NONE

  8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  CHAIR EDLER recused himself from this item due to residing within 500’ of the subject site.

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210231; ADDRESS: 11 MONTECILLO DRIVE,
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES; APPLICANT: PETER SMITH ON BEHALF OF THE JACK
  KRAMER CLUB; DESCRIPTION: A request to approve a Conditional Use Permit (CUP-
  210232) to amend CUP-102-87, revising the parking requirement methodology to be
  consistent with current standards. There are no proposed expansions to existing facilities
  or programming schedules.

  Planning Manager Naughton presented Planning Application No PA-210231 summarizing the staff
  report. In 1971, a Variance was adopted to permit the ratio of parking spaces to 1 parking space
  per 3.5 members. In 1987, the club requested an amendment to the CUP to add approximately
  1,300 sq. ft. of building area to the site. The same parking requirement carried through, but for
  unknown reasons, there were fewer on-site parking spaces than those shown on the site plans in
  the 1960’s and 1970’s. At the time there were 74 parking spaces, which coincides with the
PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, NOVEMBER 1, 2021
  1
   membership cap of 259 members. The sole reason for adding the special condition for membership
  cap was to memorialize that there were 74 on-site parking spaces.

  In 2011, Tract no. 52214 came through for entitlements, which included 12 single-family residential
  lots and Lot 13, which retained the zoning of Commercial Recreation. The Tract map was recorded
  in 2013 and sometime after recordation, the club acquired this property. Historically, prior to the
  single- family subdivision, the Butcher family had allowed The Jack Kramer Club (JKC) to use this
  parcel as overflow parking. This parcel is approximately 26,000 sq. ft. and adds to the parking
  capabilities of the site.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that according to the survey that was provided to staff, there
  are currently 66 on-site parking spaces. The club also prepared a draft of additional parking spaces
  that could be added to the site if the overflow parcel were improved and striped as a parking lot.
  The club also provided staff with their current operating program and the club is not proposing any
  expansion of their operating program and have actually reduced their operating program with the
  exclusion of their summer camps. There are no proposals for expansion of any facilities and no
  expansion of their programming. Planning Manager Naughton provided an overview of their larger
  events.

  Planning Manager Naughton provided RHEMC Section 17.22.050.F., which states that off-street
  parking shall be sufficient for the specific use. Parking requirements are based on the use of the
  site, the size of the buildings and the way the building’s function. To provide an example, the most
  recent land use with similar entitlements was the Rolling Hills Country Club and The Residences
  at Rolling Hills Country Club in 2011. At the time, the same analysis was done.

  Planning Manager Naughton provided an overview of the Parking Demand Analysis prepared by
  the City’s Traffic Engineer who utilized the Institute of Transportation Engineer’s (ITE) manuals for
  the specific land use codes. In this analysis, two additional tennis courts were used that are
  currently owned by RHCC in case the JKC acquires these in the future. The areas looked at for
  this analysis were, the number of tennis courts, the peak parking demand rate for that use, and the
  gym and fitness areas. In addition, the land use code 491, which looks at tennis courts also looks
  at ancillary facilities such as swimming pools and snack bars.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that with this request, staff is recommending that the CUP be
  amended to utilize the objective criteria, basing the parking analysis on ITE standards. Using this
  requirement would mean that City would be applying the code requirement consistent with other
  similar uses. There is nothing in the code that requires any type of membership cap for any club or
  gym type use, and no club of this type has a membership cap in the City. If the overflow lot were
  improved to be used as a parking lot, there would be a total of 114 parking spaces for the site

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff is recommending additional conditions to the CUP,
  which includes obtaining a Special Event Permit for annual events that will require a parking
  management plan for overflow parking that may not be accommodated by their improved lot. Staff
  has recommended that the club record a lot tie agreement between Lot 13 and 11 Montecillo Drive
  so that the lot be maintained at all times for the purposes of parking. This lot tie agreement can be
  removed at any time. The applicant would prefer not to encumber the property. Staff is amenable
  to revising this to be a condition of approval rather than a lot tie agreement if the Planning
  Commission agrees that this is appropriate. Staff recommends that language be added that this
  lot may not be used for storage of materials or supplies. Staff recommends that additional
  landscaping be added to the west and south side of Lot 13 to provide a buffer to the single-family
  homes along Casaba Road. Staff is also requesting that the Planning Commission consider
  whether they would like to add a condition requiring that Lot 13 be improved and striped for parking
  purposes. Staff has received correspondence from the Montecillo HOA that they would not be in
  favor of this lot being improved. The applicant is also not interested in improving this as a parking
  lot considering the expense to improve it.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff received numerous correspondence on this item.
  They have been included with the staff report and those received after the agenda were forwarded
  to the Planning Commission.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that several conditions were suggested from the
  correspondence, some of which include: three-rail fencing around the site, additional landscaping
  around the site perimeter, securing the site with a gate when the club is not in use and lighting
  improvements to reduce off-site glare.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission, open
  the public hearing, take public testimony, discuss the issues, close the public hearing, and adopt
  Resolution No. PA-210231 with a modified condition #3 as described, granting a Conditional Use
  Permit (CUP-210232) to amend CUP-102-87, revising the parking requirement methodology to be
  consistent with current standards.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, NOVEMBER 1, 2021
  2
   COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that RHEMC Section 17.22.050 is vague and asked about
  the Traffic Engineer’s standards and how have they been adopted. Planning Manager Naughton
  stated that the consistent way that staff implements parking requirements when the code does not
  provide specific details, is by using an objective standard, which is using the ITE manuals. Staff
  also looks at similar uses and applies the same methodology.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if the Planning Director would be able to change this.
  Director Wahba stated that this is not something that would be changed and would continue to look
  at the specific use as the code implies.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if there are clubs or gyms near residential areas similar to
  the JKC. Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Rolling Hills Country Club is surrounded by
  single-family homes, and the Bay Club and Equinox are located in the commercial district and there
  is residential nearby.

  COMMISSIONER YOO stated that the staff report notes that the programming schedule
  determines the parking spaces and asked if the city maintains or approves the programming
  schedule for the club. Planning Manager Naughton stated that the programming schedule would
  be taken into account when looking at parking needs for a specific use. The reason staff is
  requesting a condition to obtain a Special Event Permit for larger events is so the club can develop
  a parking management plan when the attendees would exceed the existing parking capacity.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked if they make changes to the programming schedule would the city
  need to approve the changes. Planning Manager Naughton stated that if the club were to make
  major changes to their programming schedule, they would need to amend their CUP.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT asked for a description of a major change. Planning Manager Naughton
  stated that major changes would be adding their summer camps program, larger events at a higher
  frequency, or increases in classes or group activities.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if staff receives complaints about traffic from the club.
  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff does not receive complaints about traffic related to
  the JKC. Director Wahba stated that the only complaints were years ago when larger events were
  happening, but complaints about traffic from the club are very rare.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that there is some traffic from the club but most of the traffic is from
  the neighborhood at peak hours from residents leaving and returning from work/school.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that she requested the traffic incident reports from the
  Sheriff’s Department on reported collisions on Palos Verdes Drive North from Palos Verdes Drive
  East to Rolling Vista from January 1, 2016 to August 6, 2021. There were a total of five accidents
  at Palos Verdes Drive North and Montecillo Drive, one in 2020, two in 2019 and two in 2016. There
  was also one accident in 2016 about 280 ft. east of Montecillo Drive. They were not major
  accidents.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated that in Section 4, it may be worth adding that nothing be stored
  on the lot as far as building material or other elements used for operation purposed of the club.
  There was also considerable conversation between the parties regarding time periods of use, and
  stated that any modification or suggestion of barriers between the club and residents should be
  natural.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that six events refer to overflow parking and asked if this refers to
  overflow parking in the unpaved lot and not off-site. Planning Manager Naughton stated that this is
  correct. If the Commission adopted the resolution as proposed, the club would need to obtain
  Special Event Permits for the six annual events and they would have to detail the number of
  attendees, the hours, and the highest number of cars anticipated at one time.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT asked what the unpaved lot could be used for and is there prohibition on
  unpaved parking. Planning Manager Naughton stated that there is no prohibition; there are
  requirements for minimum landscaping. The lot has the same property development standards as
  the JKC. If structures were proposed, there would be minimum building setbacks, maximum lot
  coverage, etc. If they were to utilize it as parking, they would need to landscape a minimum of 20%
  of the total site area. Director Wahba added that if they do anything other than parking, they will
  need to bring it to the Planning Commission for review.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that the Parking Demand Analysis only designate five parking spaces
  for non-tennis court users and stated that the pool is the next highest use at the club and believes
  that the Parking Demand Analysis does not reflect this. Planning Manager Naughton stated that
  when using the land use code, the more conservative 87th percentile number was used. Traffic
  Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided an overview of the ITE parking generation rate and why this

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, NOVEMBER 1, 2021
  3
   land use was used for the Parking Demand Analysis. Director Wahba suggested looking at a swim
  club, such as South End. COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER added that in the summer months the
  pool is utilized more than the tennis courts.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that there are residents of Montecillo who are concerned about parking
  demand and traffic and feels that this analysis needs to be fair.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that a breakdown of the swim memberships was provided
  in the chat. Planning Manager Naughton stated that she was not aware of this breakdown
  previously.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN inquired about events that would require a Special Event Permit. If
  someone proposed to put a tent in the parking lot, which would limit parking on this site; is there
  somewhere that states that no other uses will be approved for the lot other than parking. Planning
  Manager Naughton stated that there is no specific requirement that outlines that, but the site does
  need to maintain the required parking spaces for the use. As part of the Special Event Permit, they
  would need to show where they will accommodate the lost parking spaces. COMMISSIONER
  CARMAN asked how the noise, duration of event, and timing of such an event be controlled so
  that the community could have reassurance that it would not add to the activity level. Planning
  Manager Naughton stated that typically these events are for a specified duration, the City reaches
  out to the various agencies for review and approval as required and conditions would be added to
  the use of the Special Event Permit. Currently, there is no requirement that there be outside
  notification but this is something that could be added to the Special Event Permit application.
  COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated that this would be prudent. Director Wahba added that
  consultation with the HOA should also be added to the application.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT asked if the club has had events that are not tennis or swimming events.
  Director Wahba stated that he is not aware of any.

  In response to a question by VICE CHAIR SCOTT, Director Wahba stated that the Special Event
  Permit is a discretionary permit at the staff level.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked with the various memberships, has the club worked around
  the cap of 259 memberships. Planning Manager Naughton stated that the membership number
  was related to the 74 parking spaces they had on site at the time and the parking requirement ratio
  of 1:3.5 members and that it was the only tie to the 259 members. Today there are only 66 parking
  spaces. VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that the memberships does not relate to usage in any
  significant way.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked what would trigger that the overflow lot be required to be paved.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that the applicant and community does not want it paved and stated
  that there is a runoff problem in Montecillo that will get worse if the lot is paved. Planning Manager
  Naughton stated that if the parking requirement was reanalyzed and it was determined that the
  parking was not sufficient for the use, then it would be required that the lot be improved to be able
  to meet the number of required parking spaces.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated that she has not seen any concerns from the community about
  street parking.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER CARMAN to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, VICE CHAIR SCOTT so moved.

  David Bradley, Member of the Board of Directors’ of the JKC, stated that the club is committed to
  be a good neighbor of the community and want to continue to offer a world class tennis club in the
  City, including supporting the City’s Tracy Austin Tennis Tournament. In an effort to help put the
  club in a good financial footing they would like to have the option to raise the number of equity
  members. Mr. Bradley stated that the club currently has 13 tennis courts and the 2 tennis courts
  adjacent to the club, although they would like to have those, to date the Rolling Hills Country Club
  is not willing to sale them to the JKC. In advance of this meeting, the club has met with the
  community and the Montecillo HOA to try to come to an agreement on their concerns. Some of the
  concerns were with lighting changes and they went out and immediately changed them to be
  unidirectional and replaced the halogen lights with LED lights. They have no issue with adding
  screening around the overflow parking lot for visual as well as sound issues. In the past, there has
  been limited storage in the overflow parking; most recently, it has been furniture that was removed
  to provide for social distancing requirements due to COVID. Also, during tennis court maintenance
  there was sealant and paint temporarily stored there, but it is not meant for long-term storage.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, NOVEMBER 1, 2021
  4
   Currently, the parking lot is used for overflow parking and it is chained-off when not in use. If there
  was an event larger than what could be accommodated on-site, then arrangements would be made
  to use the Rolling Hills Covenant Church overflow parking lot. There are no plans to allow tents in
  the overflow parking area.

  Mr. Bradley stated that the JKC is a small private equity tennis club and there is a pool where there
  are five lanes of lap swimming, there is a deeper end with diving boards. The pool is mostly used
  during hot summer when it is too hot to play tennis. He stated that it would be very rare to have a
  large draw for the pool and tennis courts, simutaneously. There is a very small gym which was
  converted from an office and storage area.

  Mr. Bradley stated that for programming he would like to see that the same constraints be placed
  on Rolling Hills Country Club be placed on the JKC. Their size is much larger and they have a
  banquet hall, which the JKC does not have.

  Mr. Bradley stated that in reading through the resolution, he has the following comments.

  •  The Special Use Permit trigger be changed from 100 to 150 people.
  •  He would request to not formalize the lot tie. If the JKC were to apply for a loan, having the
  two parcels separate would make the valuation greater.
  •  In regard to paving the overflow lot, they are committed to mitigating the runoff. Keeping
  the lot in the current state, with wood chips, allows for the maximum amount of percolation.
  He added that the lot is not used often and would prefer not to use the capital to improve it.

  Mr. Bradley stated that he looks forward to working with the community and City staff.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT inquired about whether there was an attempt to sell the club. Mr. Bradley
  stated that there was an unsolicited offer made to the JKC by the Bay Club Corporation. There
  were meetings to discuss it,there was a club vote, and it was voted down. The vote was about 65%
  no and about 35% yes, that wanted to sell it.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT asked about the membership turnover. Mr. Bradley stated that it varies, but
  around the time when the Bay Club sale was turned down, some of the members from the 1960’s
  and 1970’s who no longer used their memberships were turned over to younger families in the
  community.

  Rudy Svorinich, Resident, thanked the commissioners and staff for their service to the City. Mr.
  Svorinich stated that he commends the leadership of the JKC for taking time to meet with the HOA
  and adjacent neighbors in trying to work some of their issues and their willingness to work together.
  Prior to them being in charge, there was a long period of time when the leadership of the JKC was
  not as responsive to the neighbors. As part of the memo sent to the City and responses sent to the
  City via email by his neighbors and HOA, Mr. Svorinich stated that they would like to make sure
  that going forward, the sanctity of their residential neighborhood be preserved. He stated that in
  order to do this, regardless of who is charge of the JKC, the way to accomplish this is to add specific
  conditions in the CUP. Mr. Svorinich requested that the Planning Commission continue this item to
  a future meeting to allow staff to review the methodology that has been used as the industry
  standard and stated that this methodology has not been adopted by the City Council or the
  Planning Commission. Mr. Svorinich stated that this is a methodology that can be utilized but not
  one that has to be embraced and noted the example of the Bay Club and Equinox which are both
  in commercial areas. Rolling Hills Country Club uses an activities-based methodology that has not
  been a happy resolution to the neighbors in that area. Mr. Svorinich stated that he does not believe
  that an industry standard must be used and should be looked at on a case-by-case basis. Mr.
  Svorinich requested that the Planning Commission continue this item to allow the community and
  the JKC to discuss this further and that staff look into using a number cap that everyone can agree
  to, and that some of the behavioral, ambience and operations that better reflect present day usage
  be considered. Mr. Svorinich stated that if there is an opportunity for the JKC, HOA, and neighbors
  can work something out, then it would be the right thing to do.

  Mr. Howard Edelson, VP Montecillo HOA, stated that HOA President could not be present due to
  a business trip. Mr. Edelson stated that the Montecillo HOA are in support of the JKC and its efforts
  and understands its value to the community. However, the HOA is vehemently opposed to the
  activities-based methodology and support a specific membership cap. Mr. Edelson stated that the
  Casaba HOA is also opposed to the activities-based methodology and would support a specific
  membership cap. Mr. Edelson requested that the Planning Commission consider that this item be
  continued to the next meeting to allow the HOA and the JKC could come to a mutually agreeable
  number that preserves health and financial stability of the club and the quality of the HOA.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that there have been comments opposed to the activities base
  methodology and there is discussion with the JKC and the Montecillo and Casaba HOA’s to agree
  on a membership cap. Since there is no immediate need to make a decision, more time may be
PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, NOVEMBER 1, 2021
  5
   necessary for the JKC, Montecillo and Casaba HOA and neighbors to discuss and agree on a
  proposal. Mr. Bradley stated that he would be happy to continue discussion with the HOAs and the
  community and stated that he believes that there is a disconnect with what staff wants to
  recommend based on current standards and what the JKC would agree to. Mr. Bradley stated that
  even if they could come to an agreement with the HOAs, he does not believe that this will be
  consistent with staff’s recommendation. VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that the JKC is against the lot
  lines with quite a few homes and if there could be a mutual agreement on an approach that makes
  sense, then it could override the attempt to find the objective standard. Mr. Bradley stated that the
  club could agree with a member cap of 325, which is a number has been discussed with the HOAs
  and this discussion can be continued. He does not foresee that this number will be reached.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT asked if staff has any issue with this type of approach. Planning Manager
  Naughton stated that the membership cap came from a ratio of one parking space per 3.5 members
  based on the assumption that the JKC would never acquire additional land area to provide parking
  spaces. If the Planning Commission would like to keep the ratio as the clubs parking requirement,
  the capacity of the overflow lot would be multiplied by the resulting number of on-site parking spaces
  by 3.5 members. If the draft plan were accurate and 48 parking spaces could be accommodated in
  the overflow lot, that would mean that they could have 399 members. The existing membership cap
  was not based on anything other than the existing parking spaces at the time. If the club and the
  HOA’s were to come to a private agreement on a membership cap that would be fine, but the City
  would not be comfortable requiring any kind of membership cap. Membership caps are not a
  requirement in the Municipal Code and have not been required on any other similar uses in the City.

  Assistant City Attorney Thuyen stated that Conditional Use Permits are usually imposed because
  there is some type of use that has to be conditioned to be consistent with what the code required at
  the time and what the compatible land uses were. Staff’s research notes that the issue with parking
  and membership was one way of having some type of reasonable relationship between the number
  of people using the facility and that particular issue. If the JKC would like to continue to use this
  calculation, it is within their right. However, in terms of whether it is a current requirement to address
  any current impact as identified by the Municipal Code, there is no membership cap code
  requirement. There are parking alternatives that seem more accurate to address those impacts
  presented by the club. Staff’s recommendation is to use this newer methodology that may be more
  directly tied to the impact on parking. As a legal requirement, the impact has to be related to an
  impact presented by the club; the parking methodology presented by staff does address that.
  Comments about a membership cap alone would create some concern for the City.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT asked if the current approach is extended forward and there is an agreed upon
  membership cap that the applicant voluntarily enters into and the community supports, and the
  Municipal Code does not mention membership requirements, is there any reason why it cannot be
  an enforceable City standard. Assistant City Attorney Thuyen stated that if the applicant wants to
  agree to that as a way to address the original parking impact then that was the way it was in the
  original CUP. However, the question was whether we as a City can insist upon that, if the issue is
  not to follow the original methodology.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT asked if the 3.5 can be dropped and instead have a mutually agreed upon
  membership cap.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked if the concern is that a membership cap cannot be put on a
  membership count. If the business is sold and the new business gets sold to a larger operation, now
  you have a parking facility that does not match the membership numbers.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that consideration needs to be given to what might happen
  in the future and there needs to be a rule that is applicable to other uses.

  Mr. Bradley stated that if the club was sold and the operation changed, then the new owners would
  need to come back to the Planning Commission to change their CUP to allow another use.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that he is concerned that the club can have 259 equity
  members, but could have 1,000 swim members and asked why only equity members are being
  counted. Mr. Bradley stated that there would never be a usage that would be inconsistent with the
  neighborhood and does not see this would be a problem.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT suggested that the Planning Commission continue this meeting to the
  December 6, 2021 Planning Commission meeting, that the applicant work with the Montecillo and
  Casaba HOAs to bring back a program that both sides support, that the City Attorney review any
  reason why a membership cap, devoid of parking count, is a problem for the City.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that it is a problem because there is no membership cap for any
  other use in the City. VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that it is by mutual agreement by the parties
  involved and the City supporting that agreement. Assistant City Attorney Thuyen stated that the
